text:
G-quadruplex (G4)-forming sequences, including telomeres, act as replication fork barriers; homologous recombination (HR) stabilizes/restarts stalled forks and repairs double-strand breaks. G-rich telomeric repeat replication efficiency dropped significantly in HR-lacking cells. The G4-stabilizer pyridostatin (PDS) increased telomere fragility in BRCA2-deficient cells, indicating G4 formation drives telomere instability. PDS reduced proliferation of HR-defective cells by inducing double-strand break accumulation, checkpoint activation and deregulated G2/M progression, extending to HR-defective cells with olaparib resistance via loss of 53BP1 or REV7, highlighting G4-stabilizing drugs against HR-compromised tumors.

Separately, psoralen-induced interstrand cross-links (ICLs, via photoactivated HMT) caused chromosome breakage and a 4N delay only after S-phase passage; G2-introduced ICLs caused neither G2/M arrest nor breakage, and G1 ICLs no G1/S arrest — replication is required. Primary human fibroblasts removed ~2,500 ICLs/genome at ~11 ICLs/genome/h.
